correctness.rationale: The finite count is correct: subtract the maximum enforced multiplicity independently for each permitted part. Each integer layer j is supported precisely on allowed sizes through max_(r≥j)t_r, so the resulting weight is S. This is reversible, including n=0 and S>n. RESULT.md lines 47–55 omit the complex-sector hypothesis of corrected Ingham; the radial estimate plus coefficient monotonicity would not suffice alone. The missing estimate holds here. Write P(z)=prod_(a≥1)(1−exp(−az))^(−1); Dedekind inversion gives P(z)=sqrt(z/(2π)) exp(π²/(6z)−z/24)P(4π²/z) on Re z>0. Hence P(z)/P(ell z)=ell^(−1/2) exp(μ_ell/z+(ell−1)z/24)(1+O(exp(−c/|z|))) as z→0 in each fixed sector |Im z|≤Δ Re z. Since Re(1/z)≤1/|z|, this gives the correct sector bound of Bringmann–Jennings-Shaffer–Mahlburg Theorem 1.1, with γ=μ_ell, λ=ell^(−1/2) and both power/log exponents zero. Multiplication by the allowed part 1 shows coefficients are nondecreasing; the analytic product has radius at least one. Thus the asserted coefficient asymptotic holds, with the missing hypothesis verified independently. Taylor expanding sqrt(n−S) for S=O(sqrt n) gives the claimed ratio and rate. The floors and arithmetic progression omission give A_ell(t)=(1−1/ell)t²/2+O(t+1), including zero thresholds. Independent exponentials have exactly the stated suffix-max survivor after squaring, and continuous coordinate marginals imply weak convergence via orthant inclusion–exclusion; this is not a proof of exact coincidence probabilities.
